_notes: Curation for generate_b757_map.py: what the cockpit XML cannot say, kept in one visible place.
exclude_banners: vendor banner comments whose controls are left out (circuit breakers, CDU keys, furniture, effects).
exclude_nodes: single controls left out. A name the package does not have is an error, so a stale entry cannot hide.
panels: vendor banner -> app panel name, or {name, section} when the node prefix would pick the wrong section.

node_panels: first matching {banner?, prefix?} rule wins over the banner table; {panel, section?}. A node otherwise lands in the section its prefix names (a B757_OVHD_ node in the Overhead), so a rule that moves it to another section says which.

panel_order: section -> panel names, the order the panels of that section are tabbed. The listed panels come first, in that order; the panels not listed follow alphabetically, and the run names them (a panel BlueBird adds later turns up there). A section the map does not have, a panel the section has none of, a repeat and an empty list are errors.

control_order: panel -> node names, the order the controls of that panel are tabbed. The listed controls come first, in that order; the rest follow in cockpit order. A panel no control is on, a node that is not in that panel, a repeat and an empty list are errors. Labels are made first, in cockpit order, so an order never renames or renumbers a control.
labels: node -> label, where the node name or the vendor's tooltip is wrong or unhelpful.

positions: node -> position names in value order (one per value: the names are laid onto the control's own values, so two names for a control whose values are 0 and 11 name 0 and 11), or explicit [{value, label}] when the extractor counts a value the click code never rests on (the start selectors never write 2, the chronometer ET lever skips it).

kinds: node -> toggle or button, for a control whose click code the extractor misreads. Two re-readings only: a momentary button made a toggle (its click sets its own state var by a gate, not a flip) and a select made a button (a radio-style choice that is only ever pressed). Only the kind changes (and with it the positions the generator derives: two for a toggle, none for a button, unless positions names them); the state var and the click code stay the vendor's, verbatim. The rules decide first, on the row as the extractor read it, so an entry never brings back a control they drop: it changes nothing and is only reported, like a label for a dropped node. An entry for a node the package does not have, for a control the extractor already reads that way, for any other re-reading, or for a kind the control cannot be built as (a toggle needs an L:var state), is an error.

guarded: node -> {state_var, positions, guard, guard_closed, close_sets}: a switch whose vendor click only runs while its guard is open. The extractor writes that gate as an '[if <test>] ' note in front of the click code, which is not RPN, so none of the click is kept: the control is emitted as a switch on state_var with the named positions (laid onto the control's own values, as under positions), the guard's node, the value the guard reads while closed (guard_closed) and the value closing it writes to the control (close_sets, null when closing leaves it alone), and press, release, cw and ccw are empty: the app opens the guard, writes the position and closes the guard. The guard keeps its own row. An entry takes in a control the rules leave out (the emergency lights switch) or re-reads one they keep (the stab trims), and the run names each; it never overrides exclude_nodes or an excluded banner. It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a mistyped fact or a change of BlueBird's stops the run: the click writes state_var, its gate reads the guard's var, and the guard's own click writes close_sets to the control. An entry for a node or a guard the package does not have, names that do not fit the vendor's count of positions, a positions or kinds entry for the same node, and any other control whose click code carries the gate note are errors.

direct_write: list of nodes whose vendor click code the map leaves out: the control is emitted as the rules build it (state var, kind, label, panel and positions unchanged, the positions still checked against what the vendor's code writes) and press, release, cw and ccw are empty, so the app writes the state var to the picked position, as it does for any switch with no click code. For a switch whose code cannot take a pick where it aims and writes nothing but its own L:var (the chronometer ET levers). It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a change of BlueBird's stops the run instead of reaching the app: the click code must exist (else the entry does nothing), carry no gate note (a gated click belongs under guarded, which opens the guard first) and write nothing but the state var (another L:var, a K: or an H: event would no longer run). The run names each, and what it left out. An entry for a node the package does not have or the map does not keep, a node also under guarded or kinds, a control that is not a switch or has no state var or no positions, and a click code that fails those checks are errors.

keep_without_node: list of nodes kept although neither cockpit model has a node of that name. The generator reads the node names of the package's two interior models, BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR.gltf and BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR.gltf (it stops when either is missing), and leaves out every control the other rules keep whose node is in neither: a switch the cockpit does not have is noise to a pilot who cannot find it, and the run names each one. A control one model alone has says which, with (PW) or (RR) at the end of its label unless the label already does (L Fuel Control (PW)); a label that names the wrong variant stops the run. An entry here keeps a control BlueBird's published list proves real, and the run names each; it stays empty unless that list proves one. An entry for a node the package does not have, for a node a model has (it does nothing), for a node also in exclude_nodes or for one the rules leave out for another reason is an error, and so is a guarded or include_nodes entry for a node no cockpit has that this list does not keep. A direct_write entry for one stops the run until it is removed, and a kinds, labels or positions entry for one changes nothing and is only reported.
spelling: vendor words repaired wherever a label is made from them (US English, vendor typos).
status: read-only L:vars the app can speak or show; positions are names for 0, 1, 2 ...

B757_OVHD_CABINALT_SWITCH is excluded (label kept for later): its turn code writes 0 and 7, every vendor panel-state snapshot rests it at 4, and the vendor's OFF/AUTO/ON tips are a copy-paste. Its positions are unknown; revisit in the sim.

B757_OVHD_L_ENG_START_SWITCH and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_START_SWITCH: the extractor counts 6 positions, but the click code computes its values and never writes 2 (cw goes 1 to 3, ccw 3 to 1), so the list is explicit pairs without 2. All 9 vendor panel-state snapshots hold both selectors at 3, the manual's normal position is AUTO, and engine start is GND, which is ccw of AUTO. 4 OFF, 5 CONT and 6 FLT are BlueBird's names (its simvar list, cited below); unmeasured in the sim.

A banner with no entry under panels is not guessed: it is printed as a note (unmapped_banners) unless a node_panels rule names its controls. The four BBS_fuelcut_* switches (one banner is '(no banner)') are named by a node rule.

include_nodes: single controls taken in from an excluded banner BY NODE; the banner stays excluded and its other controls stay out, and the panel and section come from a node_panels rule. A name the package does not have, a node also in exclude_nodes, a node no excluded banner hides and a node the rules still drop are errors. In: BBS757_PEDESTAL_Park_Brake_Lever, BBS757_SPOILERDOWN_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERARMED_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERUP_CLICK (banner RIGHT WINDOW RAIN EFFECTS); ENGINE_Switch_ATDisc_1 (the left TO/GA button only; ENGINE_Switch_ATDisc_2 is not taken in) and B757_AT_DISC_1 (banner THROTTLES MAIN; B757_AT_DISC_2 is not taken in). All sit in Pedestal / Control stand, in file order.

EVIDENCE for the control stand and the position names below (2026-10-25). preset = the nine vendor panel states in Data/panel_states/*.snap (cold and dark, turnaround, before start, ready for taxi, ready for takeoff, after takeoff, cruise, approach, final approach; positional arrays, but most knob states also sit in them as named L:var pairs). manual = BlueBird's v1.01 User Procedures and Complete Flight Guide. measured = read live in the sim (docs/b757/evidence/live-findings.md). unmeasured = no live read: the name rests on the sources given and goes on the in-sim plan. Names are the panel's legends as printed (capitals), as the brief spells them; a list entry 'Position N' is a position nothing names.
Position names from BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21), read 2026-10-25.

PLAN 02 TASK 1 (2026-10-26): positions named from that list alone, unmeasured in the sim and with no preset or manual evidence of their own (the controls whose other notes cite the list have such evidence besides): B757_CABIN_CEILING (0 Off, 1 33%, 2 66%, 3 100%), B757_CABIN_WINDOW and B757_CABIN_ENTRY (0 Off, 1 50%, 2 100%), B757_OVHD_WARNING_IND_SWITCH (0 DIM, 11 BRT: its click code writes those two values, which the extractor takes as its positions), B757_MAIN_M_Gau_STBY_GYRO_SELECTOR (0 OFF, 1 ILS, 2 BCRS), B757_ECAM_LRAUTO_KNOB (0 L, 1 AUTO, 2 R) and B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_2, the Flight Recorder (0 ON, 1 AUTO, 2 TEST).

B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH_FO (L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, _FO): 0 RUN, 1 HOLD, 3 RESET, explicit pairs without 2. The list says RESET is 3 with 2 unused, and the click code agrees: the code that steps up from HOLD writes 3 straight from 1 ('1 == if{ 3 ...'), so no step from HOLD rests on 2. The cockpit's tooltip list (RUN, HOLD, RESET: three tips for four values) puts RESET at 2, which that code never writes; the generator stops on a list that names 2 instead, because 3 is then written outside the list. The code that steps down still passes through 2 on its way from 3 to 1; that stop has no name. B757_MAIN_CHRONO_SET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_SET_SWITCH_FO (L:BBS_CHRONO_RIGHT_SWITCH, _FO): 0 RUN, 1 HOLD, 2 Slow slew, 3 Fast slew (the list; the vendor's tips for them repeat the ET lever's RUN, HOLD, RESET and name nothing here). Both unmeasured in the sim.

B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_3 to B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_10 are the P61 test switches: their release code writes 1, so 1 is Neutral on all of them, and the list names 0 and 2, the two tests, by the switch's label: Equip Cooling (SWITCH_3) and Yaw Damp (SWITCH_4) 'Upper test' / 'Lower test'; Wing AI Window Heat (SWITCH_6) 'Wing anti-ice test' / 'Probe heat test'; Ground Prox Hyd Gen (SWITCH_7) 'Ground proximity test' / 'Hydraulic generator test'; TO and Land Config (SWITCH_8) 'Takeoff config test' / 'Landing config test'; Air Data Stall Right (SWITCH_9) and Left (SWITCH_10) 'Air data test' / 'Stall warning test'. B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_5 (Duct Leak Fuel Qty) is the one the list gives no test names: 1 Neutral, 0 and 2 stay 'Position 0' and 'Position 2'. Unmeasured in the sim.

PLAN 02 TASK 2 (2026-10-26): labels and kinds that match the cockpit, from BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml (cited as XML:line) and BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21), all unmeasured in the sim. B757_OVHD_SWITCH_GAURD is the emergency lights guard, not a passenger oxygen one: the XML says so ('OVHD SWITCH GUARD is the EMERGENCY LIGHTS GUARD', XML:11362) and passes it as the GUARD_LVAR of the emergency lights switch (BBS_B757_EMERGENCY_LIGHTS_COMPONENT, XML:8106-8110); the vendor's tip on its other row, 'RAM AIR TURBINE', and the PASS_OXY in the name of the switch it covers are copies. The list calls it 'Emergency lights guard - template and interlock', 0 = closed, 1 = open, which is what its positions say.

The hydraulic panel has two engine pumps and four electric ones. B757_OVHD_C_ENG1_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_C_ENG2_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON are the center system's two electric pumps, C1 and C2 (the 757's center system has no engine pump; the XML tips read 'C ENG1 PUMP' and 'C ENG2 PUMP', XML:7085 and 7140, and the list puts them at Left / Center and Right / Center); B757_OVHD_L_ENG_ELEC_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_ELEC_PUMPS_BUTTON are the left and right electric pumps (tips 'L ENG ELEC' and 'R ENG ELEC', XML:7030 and 7250; the list: 'Hydraulic electric pump selection'). B757_OVHD_L_ENG_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON stay the engine pumps, 'L ENG HYD Pumps' and 'R ENG HYD Pumps', made from their node names. The six labels differ, and control_order is untouched, so the electric pumps stay in the order R, C1, C2, L. B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_FWD_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_AFT_BUTTON are the fuel crossfeed valve switches, not pumps: their node names and tips say pumps (XFEED PUMP FWD and AFT, XML:8585 and 8530; the list: 'Crossfeed pumps forward button'), but the circuit breakers for the same valves are named fuel_crossfeed_valve_fwd and _aft (XML:34638, 34655).

B757_GAURD_11_SWITCH and B757_GAURD_12_SWITCH are the covers of the 1 BTL and 2 BTL cargo fire buttons: the vendor's template instances of B757_PED_1BTL_CARGOFIRE_BUTTON and B757_PED_2BTL_CARGOFIRE_BUTTON name them as their GUARD_NODE_ID (XML:15975 and 16013), so they read '1 BTL Cargo Fire Guard' and '2 BTL Cargo Fire Guard' after the buttons' own labels. The list has no row for either guard; the vendor's disabled earlier components tip them 'FWD CARGO' and 'AFT CARGO'.

B757_MCP_btn_autopilot_disengage: 0 Up, 1 Down. Its click flips its own var and passes it on to K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET ('if{ 1 (>K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET) } els{ 0 (>K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET) }'), so 1 is the bar down, which disengages the autopilot, and 0 the bar up; its animation names no positions and the list has no row for it. BBS757_THRREF_CLICK (L:BBS757_THRREF_PULL): 0 In, 1 Pulled; the list: 'Manual EPR-reference mode', 1 = pulled/manual, 0 = pushed/manual off. B757_MCP_AP_SPD_HOLD_SW writes L:B757_MCP_IAS_MACH_KNOB_BUTTON, which the list calls the 'Speed intervention command' (write 1 to request it, 0 = idle): the push of the IAS/MACH knob, so it reads 'Speed Intervene', not 'AP SPD Hold'.

BBS757_FIREHANDLE1_CLICK3, the APU fire handle, is a toggle (kinds) on L:B757_APUFIRE_SWITCH, its pulled state, as the engine handles are on L:B757_ENGFIRE_1_SWITCH and _2_ (the list: 'Apufire switch', 0 = normal, 1 = fire handle pulled): 0 In, 1 Pulled. Its click writes 1 when the handle is unlocked (L:BBS757_FIREUNLOCK3) or the APU fire is active and 0 otherwise, a gate and not a flip, so the extractor read a momentary button with no state to show; the app now reads the handle before it presses. The 14 microphone selects, B757_PED_AUDIO_1_MIC_L_LIGHT to _INT_LIGHT and the seven of B757_PED_AUDIO_2_MIC_*_LIGHT, are buttons (kinds): a click sets that microphone to 1 and the panel's other six to 0, so a combo of Off and On could never reach Off. The list calls each a 'microphone selector' (0 = deselected, 1 = selected; 'a 0-to-1 transition selects the transmitter').

PLAN 02 TASK 3 (2026-10-26): the emergency lights switch and the two stab trim cutouts are guarded, from BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml (cited as XML:line) and BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21). B757_OVHD_PASS_OXY_Toggle_Switch_CLICK is the emergency lights switch (label Emergency Lights; BBS_B757_EMERGENCY_LIGHTS_COMPONENT, XML:8106-8120; the PASS_OXY in its node name is a copy, as for its guard): its state is L:B757_OVHD_PASS_OXY_Toggle_Switch_CLICK, 0 OFF, 1 ARMED, 2 ON (the list; its click steps '1 + 2 min' and '1 - 0 max', XML:1504 and 1507, which is why the extractor read a switch with three positions, and its animation reads an O: var, which is why the rules left it out). Its guard is B757_OVHD_SWITCH_GAURD, its own L:var (XML:1361): the click runs only while that reads 1 (XML:1502), so 1 is open and 0 is closed (guard_closed 0; the list: 0 = closed, 1 = open). Closing the guard writes 1, ARMED, to the switch: the guard's click writes its RESET_VALUE 1 (XML:1375-1378 and 8118) and the switch's own update code forces 1 while the guard reads 0 (XML:1532), so close_sets is 1. B757_Stab_trim_C_toggle_switch_CLICK and B757_Stab_trim_R_toggle_switch_CLICK are the stab trim cutouts (labels Stab Trim C Cutout and Stab Trim R Cutout; BBS757_STAB_TRIM_CUTOUTS, XML:15380-15408): their states are L:B757_Stab_trim_C_toggle_switch_CLICK and L:B757_Stab_trim_R_toggle_switch_CLICK, 0 NORMAL, 1 CUTOUT (the list; the click toggles 0 and 1, XML:1426), behind B757_AISLE_STAND_STAB_1_GAURD_SWITCH and B757_AISLE_STAND_STAB_2_GAURD_SWITCH, each its own L:var (XML:1361); the click runs only while its guard reads 1 (XML:1424), and closing a guard writes its RESET_VALUE 0, NORMAL, to the switch (XML:15385 and 15393), so close_sets is 0. The extractor had read the stab trims as toggles whose press began with the gate note (not valid RPN, and its 'On' was CUTOUT). measured (docs/b757/evidence/live-findings.md, docs/b757/spec-gaps.md 3.3): the emergency lights switch reads 1 with its guard 0, the stab trims 0 with their guards 0, none changed. unmeasured in the sim: that a write to a switch's L:var takes while its guard is open (the sim's own gate is in the click, which the app no longer replays).

PLAN 02 TASK 4 (2026-10-26, ruling R10): B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH_FO are direct_write: the map holds none of their click code and the app writes L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH (_FO) to the picked value. Read from the vendor's code (BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml:26725-26735 and 28542-28552), unmeasured in the sim: the clockwise code lowers the value one step, '(L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) -- d 0 < if{ 0 } (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum)', so 3 goes to 2 to 1 to 0, and the anticlockwise code raises it but jumps HOLD straight to RESET, '(L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) 1 == if{ 3 (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) } els{ (L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) ++ d 3 > if{ 3 } (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) }', so 0 goes to 1 to 3. The positions are 0 RUN, 1 HOLD and 3 RESET, with 2 unused (BlueBird's list; task 1 left it out). The map's cw was that clockwise code, so the app's step up lowered the value; swapping cw and ccw would fix the direction and not the steps: a step down from RESET still lands on 2, which is no position, and the app then refuses every later pick. The vendor code writes nothing but that one L:var (the generator checks that on every run), so writing the picked value directly loses nothing, and it also takes a pick from a lever a cockpit click has left on 2. The positions stay checked against that code: a list that names RESET at 2 still stops the run.

PLAN 02 TASK 5 (2026-10-26, ruling R65): the map holds only controls the cockpit has. Read from the package's two interior models, BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR.gltf (3104 nodes) and BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR.gltf (3116 nodes, 3094 of them in both), by node name, whole and as written (no node of either has one of the names below in another case). Of the 425 controls the other rules kept, 395 have a node in both models, 2 in the PW model only, 6 in the RR model only and 22 in neither. In the PW model only: BBS_fuelcut_PW1 and BBS_fuelcut_PW2, whose labels already end (PW). In the RR model only: BBS_fuelcut_RR1 and BBS_fuelcut_RR2, whose labels already end (RR); B757_OVHD_L_ELEC-ENG-CONT_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ELEC-ENG-CONT_BUTTON, which now read L ELEC ENG Cont (RR) and R ELEC ENG Cont (RR); and their guards B757_GAURD_1_SWITCH and B757_GAURD_2_SWITCH, Elec Eng Cont 1 Guard (RR) and Elec Eng Cont 2 Guard (RR). In neither, so the map leaves them out: B757_EICAS_COMPUTER_KNOB (a second EICAS Computer knob: the EICAS computer switch is B757_ECAM_LRAUTO_KNOB); the five switches of the ADF panel, B757_PED_ADF_TONE_SWITCH, B757_PED_ADF_L_TEST_SWITCH, B757_PED_ADF_R_TEST_SWITCH, B757_PED_ADF_L_SWITCH and B757_PED_ADF_R_SWITCH; B757_PED_WX_R_TEST_BUTTON (the left test button has a node); the six P6 display buttons, B757_P6_DISPLAY_1_EADI_BUTTON, B757_P6_DISPLAY_1_EHSI_BUTTON, B757_P6_DISPLAY_1_EICAS_BUTTON, B757_P6_DISPLAY_2_EICAS_BUTTON, B757_P6_DISPLAY_2_EADI_BUTTON and B757_P6_DISPLAY_2_EHSI_BUTTON; the five P6 event buttons, B757_P6_EVENT_AUTO_TEST_SWITCH_BUTTON, B757_P6_EVENT_MAN_TEST_SWITCH_BUTTON, B757_P6_EVENT_MAIN_TEST_SWITCH_BUTTON, B757_P6_EVENT_REC_TEST_SWITCH_BUTTON and B757_P6_EVENT_ERASE_TEST_SWITCH_BUTTON; and B757_GAURD_13_SWITCH, B757_GAURD_14_SWITCH, B757_GAURD_15_SWITCH and B757_P61_PANEL_SWITCH_GAURD. That is the 28 controls without a node in the PW cockpit and the 24 in the RR one that docs/b757/spec-gaps.md 3.7 counts. The ADF panel held only those five switches (its tuning knobs have nodes, and are dropped as infinite knobs), so the panel is gone and its node_panels rule and its panel_order entry went with it. The six guarded switches and guards of plan 02 task 3 are in both models, and stay. keep_without_node stays empty: BlueBird's list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, read 2026-10-26) has a row for 20 of the 22, but each is a variable the XML declares, and a row does not say the control is in the cockpit. For the ADF L and R switches (0 ADF, 1 ANT, 2 OFF) it says 'Model selector position. Functional system behavior depends on its binding'; for the ADF tone and test switches and the P6 buttons 'Maintained state'; for the guards 13 to 15 (P61 left, center and right button guard) and the P61 panel cover that the XML maps the state to animation endpoints. It has no row for B757_EICAS_COMPUTER_KNOB or B757_PED_WX_R_TEST_BUTTON. Read from the package's files, not the sim.

BBS757_PEDESTAL_Park_Brake_Lever (L:B757_FC_PARK_BRAKE): 0 Released, 1 Set. A toggle whose click flips the var. measured (session 6): K:PARKING_BRAKES left the var at 1 while the stock BRAKE PARKING POSITION read 0. preset: 1 in cold and dark, before start, ready for taxi and ready for takeoff; 0 in turnaround and the four airborne states. unmeasured: releasing it with the lever click while PARKING BRAKE MODE is REALISTIC (that setting wants full pedal braking).

BBS757_SPOILERDOWN_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERARMED_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERUP_CLICK write 0, 10 and 100 to L:B757_FC_SPOILER_LEVER and keep no state of their own (buttons with a press only, replayed verbatim). measured (session 6): 10 is ARMED, 0 is down (K:SPOILERS_ARM_TOGGLE); all nine presets hold 0. unmeasured: 100 for UP (the click code only).

ENGINE_Switch_ATDisc_1 is the left TO/GA button: its press writes L:GO_AROUND_PADDLE1 and fires K:AUTO_THROTTLE_TO_GA, its release clears the var, all replayed verbatim. B757_AT_DISC_1 is the A/T disconnect: press writes L:B757_AT_DISC_1 1, release 0. unmeasured in flight.

B757_MCP_HOLD_1_BUTTON is HDG HOLD, B757_MCP_HOLD_2_BUTTON is ALT HOLD (the generated labels 'Hold 1' and 'Hold 2' were slips). Evidence: (1) the vendor's disabled original components (commented out in BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml, after the BBS757_MCP_BUTTON instances) pair HOLD_1 with H:BBS_AP_HDG_HOLD and HOLD_2 with H:BBS_AP_ALT_HOLD; (2) the template instances run LNAV, VNAV, FLCH, HOLD_1, VS, HOLD_2, BCRS_1, LOC, APP, the 757 MCP's order; (3) preset lights: L:B757_MCP_HOLD_2_BUTTON is 1 after takeoff, in cruise and on base leg and 0 on final approach, L:B757_MCP_HOLD_1_BUTTON is 0 in all nine. unmeasured live.

B757_MCP_CMD_1_BUTTON, B757_MCP_CMD_2_BUTTON, B757_MCP_CMD_3_BUTTON are CMD L, CMD C and CMD R (the generated labels 'CMD 1' to 'CMD 3' were the node numbers): the 757 MCP's three autopilot engage buttons, left to right, as the app speaks their lights ('CMD R on', plan 01 task 10b). Each button's decal lights from L:B757_MCP_CMD_n_BUTTON (bool). unmeasured live: which of the three nodes is which side (1 = L, 3 = R is the numbering's natural reading).

B757_MAIN_knob_gears_altn_autobrake (L:BBS_AUTOBRAKE_KNOB): 0 RTO, 1 OFF, 2 DISARM, 3 '1', 4 '2', 5 '3', 6 '4', 7 MAX AUTO. preset: 0 in ready for taxi and ready for takeoff (manual: the before-takeoff item AUTOBRAKES RTO); 1 in cold and dark, turnaround, before start, after takeoff and cruise (manual: AUTOBRAKES OFF after landing); 2 in approach and final approach. manual: the selector is shown 'at DISARM' with the amber AUTO BRAKES light; the vendor's landing calculator lists A/BRK 1 to 4 and MAX AUTO. unmeasured: 2 to 7. 3 to 7 follow the standard 757 selector order by elimination, and so does 2 = DISARM, although the approach presets sit on 2 where a landing setting would be expected: check by one click from OFF (the EICAS shows AUTOBRAKES on DISARM).

BBS_fuelcut_PW1, BBS_fuelcut_PW2: 0 CUTOFF, 2 RUN (a left click goes to 2, a right click to 0). preset: 0 in cold and dark, turnaround and before start; 2 in all six states after engine start; manual: the shutdown item 'Fuel control switches CUTOFF'. The RR switches are the reverse (preset 2 in the cold states, 0 once running; their tips read RUN, RICH, CUTOFF), so the two lists differ on purpose. Backed by presets and manual, not read live.

B757_IRS_L_SWITCH, B757_IRS_C_SWITCH, B757_IRS_R_SWITCH: 0 OFF, 1 ALIGN, 2 NAV, 3 ATT. preset: 0 in cold and dark, 2 in the other eight; manual: 'IRS selectors OFF, THEN NAV', and 'NAV to ALIGN to NAV' for a realignment. unmeasured: 1 ALIGN (the manual's word, in the standard slot between OFF and NAV) and 3 ATT (the standard 757 selector; the manuals never say ATT). B757_IRS_LARGE_KNOB (4 positions, 3 in every preset) and B757_IRS_CENTRE_KNOB (3 positions, 0 in every preset) are the display unit's knobs: BlueBird's simvar list names them (Large: TK/GS, PPOS, WIND, HDG/STS; Center: L, C, R); unmeasured in the sim.

B757_ADI_1_TFC_KNOB, B757_ADI_2_TFC_KNOB (ND range; L:BBS_ND1_Range_Index, L:BBS_ND2_Range_Index): 0 10 NM, 1 20 NM, 2 40 NM, 3 80 NM, 4 160 NM, 5 320 NM. B757_ADI_1_CTR_KNOB, B757_ADI_2_CTR_KNOB (ND mode): 0 VOR, 1 APP, 2 MAP, 3 PLAN. The words are the vendor's tooltip lists ('320 NM' '160 NM' ... '10 NM' 6 (L:BBS_ND1_Range_Index) case and 'PLAN' 'MAP' 'APP' 'VOR' 4 (L:B757_ADI_2_CTR_KNOB) case), read with the LAST word pushed as index 0. unmeasured: that reading of the list. For it: the FO mode knob initializes to 2 and all nine presets hold 2, which is MAP only under this reading (APP under the other), and it puts the approach presets on 80 NM (base leg) and 20 NM (final) where the other reading gives 40 and 160 NM. The manual calls the approach mode ILS; the cockpit's own word APP is kept.

B757_PED_TCAS_MODE_KNOB: 0 STBY, 1 ALT RPTG OFF, 2 XPNDR, 3 TA ONLY, 4 TA/RA (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 0 in cold and dark and turnaround, 4 in the other seven; manual: 'set transponder TA/RA ... before start', and the panel is illustrated at 'L and STBY'. unmeasured: 1 to 3 (they are the standard 757 order). B757_PED_TCAS_XPNDR_SWITCH: 0 L, 1 R; manual: 'Select L or R for the pilot flying', illustrated at L; 0 in every preset; the WASM keeps two transponders. unmeasured: which side is 0.

B757_MAIN_knob_gears_altn_flaps (8 positions): 0 NORM, 1 UP, 2 1, 3 5, 4 15, 5 20, 6 25, 7 30 (BlueBird's simvar list). 0 NORM: 0 in all nine presets and the manual's 'ALTN FLAPS SELECTOR NORM'. 1 to 7 unmeasured (its animation tips are a copy of the standby power selector's and name nothing).

RULING R32 (2026-10-25; the positions it left numbered are named since plan 02 task 1, from BlueBird's simvar list, cited below): seven controls the flows needed, named only where BlueBird's nine panel states (Data/panel_states/*.snap, order as above) and the manual's procedure text agree; every other position stayed 'Position N'. The presets and the manual still back the names below that they cover. A misnamed position would not be caught by the in-sim preset check, which reads the same values back.

B757_OVHD_SEATBELTS_SWITCH: 0 OFF, 1 AUTO, 2 ON. preset: 0 in cold and dark and turnaround, 2 in the other seven; manual: signs ON before start, OFF at shutdown. 1 (the middle position, BlueBird's AUTO) unmeasured.

B757_OVHD_NO_SMOKING_SWITCH: 0 OFF, 1 AUTO, 2 ON. preset: 2 in all nine (no state holds it off); OFF at 0 rests on the identical three-position seat belt switch beside it and the manual's signs OFF at shutdown. 1 and 0 unmeasured (1 is BlueBird's AUTO).

B757_OVHD_SEL_L_PACK_SWITCH, B757_OVHD_SEL_R_PACK_SWITCH: 0 OFF, 1 AUTO, 2 STBY N, 3 STBY C, 4 STBY W (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 0 in cold and dark, 1 in every powered state; manual: 'PACK SELECTORS ... OFF with no supply'. 2 to 4 unmeasured.
B757_OVHD_MODE_SELECT_SWITCH: 0 AUTO 1, 1 AUTO 2, 2 MAN (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 0 in all nine; manual: 'mode selector AUTO 1 or AUTO 2'. 1 and 2 unmeasured.

B757_OVHD_ENG_START_SWITCH: label Ignition (the node says ENG START, the vendor's tooltip says 'Engine Ignitors'; the panel's L and R ENG Start selectors are separate rows), 0 '1', 1 '2', 2 'BOTH' (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 0 in all nine; manual: 'Ignition 1 is the illustrated example'. 1 and 2 unmeasured.

B757_MCP_AP_HDG_BNKLIM (L:BBS757_BANK_LIMITER): 0 AUTO, 1 5, 2 10, 3 15, 4 20, 5 25 (BlueBird's simvar list: the degrees). preset: 0 in all nine; manual: 'BANK LIMIT SELECTOR ... AUTO'. 1 to 5 unmeasured.
B757_EICAS_LWR_THRUST-REF_KNOB (L:B757_EICAS_LWR_THRUST_REF_KNOB): 0 L, 1 BOTH, 2 R (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 1 in all nine; manual: 'thrust reference BOTH'. 0 and 2 unmeasured.
B757_OVHD_WIPER_SWITCH: 0 OFF, 1 LOW, 2 HIGH (BlueBird's simvar list). preset: 0 in all nine, dry weather in every state (no state runs the wipers). 1 and 2 unmeasured.

status BBS757_vis_chocks (RULING R31): 0 Removed, 1 In place, shown on the Status display and never announced. measured 2026-10-25 (live-findings.md, EFB Ground Services): the EFB's CHOCKS tile toggles it 0 to 1 to 0. preset: 1 in cold and dark and turnaround, 0 in the other seven.

RULING R37 (2026-10-25, the owner's direction after the first flight): the panels follow the manual's preflight flow and the most used controls come first in a panel (panel_order, control_order). The lists are the owner's to adjust; a control_order lists only the controls that lead, and the rest keep cockpit order. The three start selectors (Ignition, L ENG Start, R ENG Start: nodes B757_OVHD_ENG_START_SWITCH, B757_OVHD_L_ENG_START_SWITCH, B757_OVHD_R_ENG_START_SWITCH, banner LIGHT OVERRIDE) and the four fuel control switches (BBS_fuelcut_PW1, PW2, RR1, RR2) share one Pedestal panel, Engines, in start order: Ignition, L ENG Start, L Fuel Control (PW), R ENG Start, R Fuel Control (PW), then the RR pair. The three node_panels rules for the start selectors name the section Pedestal, because a B757_OVHD_ node otherwise lands in the Overhead by its prefix. TCAS and transponder lists TCAS Mode first; the app adds its Squawk Code field right after it (BBS757Definition.Readouts.cs). Each EFIS panel leads with ND Mode and ND Range.
_suspected_slips: Information only, never applied: press / release / cw / ccw are the vendor's click code verbatim, because the app replays exactly what the cockpit click runs. The generator prints the same list as suspected_slips.

B757_OVHD_L_PUMPS_AFT_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_L_PUMPS_FWD_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_AFT_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_FWD_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_R_PUMPS_AFT_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_R_PUMPS_FWD_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_C_PUMPS_L_BUTTON, B757_OVHD_C_PUMPS_R_BUTTON: press ends '! (L:<node>_ON,bool) ! (>B757_..._ON,bool)': a set with no 'L:' in front (and a '!' with nothing to negate) in the vendor's XML.
